I know most aren't avid Anime watchers but Ghost in the Shell (GITS) is an absolute classic scifi tale that would be enjoyable by most (BINGE IT ON NETFLIX), but I digress.

Ghost in the Shell is a story of politics and computerized warfare set in a future when the world stablized after a global conflict. Corporate entities and Governments are seamlessly intertwined, computers augment humans in ways such that they are impossible to excise, an entire generation was lost to the net and fell into a VR fantasy world from which they never return. The story has deep philosophical ponderings about technology, like "How can we know what is real if our technology that augment us can fabricate memories?" and "What makes a human a human and a robot a robot, where do the over lap? Can they over lap?". To me 1984 is so outlandish and romanticly sinister that it strikes me as too implausible to happen (but it makes for a good bedtime story to scare teenagers to sleep). For me Ghost in the Shell presents a more plausible subtle dystopia that's slight enough that most don't notice it has completely immersed all aspects of society.

Does the future that Ghost in the Shell takes place in seem like a more plausible future than Orwell's nightmare?
GITS vs 1984. Which seems more plausible?
If a future of GITS means I get to see Kusanagi's nice ass in those tights, I'll take GITS anyday.
